page.layout: One page of text in a single column, running full width. No marginal notes, no footnotes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword at lower right, gathering signature at lower left.

main_text.p: subter te, ferrea. 24.Dabit Iehouah pluviam terrae tuae pulverem & cineres, è coelis descendet super te, donec disperdaris.
Psalm.107.33. Redigit flumina in desertum, & scaturigines aquarum in sitim.
34.Terram fructiferā in falsuginem: propter maliciam habitantium in ea. 35.Redigit desertum in stagnū aquarum, & terram solitudinis in scaturigines aquarū.

Nota est historia, de coelo per triennīu & sex menses ad preces Eliæ Prophetæ claufo, ne plueret, temporibus Achab Regis Israelis: & de fame, quæ siccitatem & [illegible, ~8 letters] illam est secuta: 1.Regū 17.& 18. Iac.5.17.18.

Secundò mysterium. alias enim parca manu, alias larga, verbum Dei, ceu pluvia irrigans, & potus recreans animas nostras, nobis coceditur: interdum autem iusto Dei iudicio denegatur ingratis. Iu-xta hæc dicta:
Ifaiæ 30.20.Dabit vobis Dominus panem angustum, & aquam oppressionis: sed nō elongabitur ultra doctor tuus, &c.
Ifai.55.1. Omnes sitientes venite ad aquas: etiam vos quib.non est argentum, venite, &c.

page.notes: Running head is the title as printed; the number 327 sits at top right. The Greek word after "siccitatem &" is too faint to read reliably, so it is marked illegible; it is a Greek word, not Latin. "coceditur" in the paragraph beginning "Secundò" is as printed; it may be a misprint for "conceditur" but I have not corrected it. "pluuiam" and "puluerem" are printed with u for consonant v and are given as "pluviam" and "pulverem" per the u/v rule. Some line-end joins ("denegaturingratis", "inscaturigines") were read with the space restored from the sense of the line. The catchword "Ezech." and the signature "x 4" are read from the foot of the page.
